Front: What clinical management options fall within cumulative PL3 scope (PL1 through PL3) for the Abdominal Pain guideline?
Back: Oxygen, target SpO2 92%–96%; Nausea and Vomiting Guideline as needed; 3 & 12-lead ECG placement.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to establish IV or IO access for an abdominal pain patient when indicated, per the Abdominal Pain guideline?
Back: No. IV/IO access is PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to give IV isotonic crystalloid for dehydration per the Abdominal Pain guideline?
Back: No. IV fluid with isotonic crystalloid is PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to perform ECG assessment (interpretation) per the Abdominal Pain guideline?
Back: No. ECG Assessment is PL5; PL3 and below include only 3 & 12-lead ECG placement (PL2).

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to follow the Pain Management Guideline for abdominal pain per this protocol?
Back: No. Pain Management Guideline as needed is PL5.

Front: What clinical management options fall within cumulative PL3 scope (PL1 through PL3) for Airway Management (Adult & Pediatric 2022)?
Back: BLS foreign body airway obstruction evaluation/removal; NPA and/or OPA with BVM ventilation; oxygen including passive apneic oxygenation 25 L/min via nasal cannula; SpO2 monitoring; BIAD (e.g., i-gel); EtCO2 monitoring; 12-lead ECG placement and acquisition.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to establish IV or IO access during general airway management per this guideline?
Back: No. IV/IO access is PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to intubate, perform video laryngoscopy intubation, or needle/surgical cricothyrotomy per this airway guideline?
Back: No. Advanced airway procedures (intubation, cricothyrotomy, etc.) are PL5–PL6.

Front: What PL3-appropriate action applies if a suction catheter cannot be passed in a tracheostomy patient (Tracheostomy Airway Management 2022)?
Back: Ventilate from the mouth with standard airway management while covering the stoma.

Front: What clinical management options fall within cumulative PL3 scope (PL1 through PL3) for Tracheostomy Airway Management (Adult & Pediatric 2022)?
Back: Apply high-flow oxygen to tracheostomy and face; remove speaking cap if present; BVM to tracheostomy with inner cannula (or pediatric mask if unable); if no chest rise, block stoma with wet gauze and BVM on face; SpO2 monitoring; troubleshoot easily correctible causes; if ventilator problem, remove from ventilator and BVM; CPR if no pulse; EtCO2 monitoring; 12-lead ECG placement and acquisition; if suction catheter cannot be passed—ventilate from mouth while covering stoma.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to perform tracheal suctioning per the tracheostomy guideline?
Back: No. Tracheal suctioning is PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to place IV/IO or inflate the tracheostomy cuff with air/saline for profuse bleeding per this guideline?
Back: No. IV/IO and cuff management for profuse bleeding are PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to remove/replace a blocked tracheostomy tube or perform oral intubation through the stoma per this guideline?
Back: No. Tube change, oral intubation/replace stoma with ETT, and related steps are PL5.

Front: What clinical management options fall within cumulative PL3 scope (PL1 through PL3) for Allergic Reaction / Anaphylaxis?
Back: Assist with patient epinephrine autoinjector for severe respiratory distress/anaphylaxis; epinephrine if patient has none; oxygen target SpO2 92–96%; cold pack to bite/sting and remove bee stinger if present; basic airway management; albuterol; diphenhydramine adult PO only; CPAP if refractory to albuterol; monitor EtCO2.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to establish IV or IO access for anaphylaxis when indicated?
Back: No. IV/IO access is PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to run IV isotonic crystalloid resuscitation for hypotension per the Anaphylaxis guideline?
Back: No. IV fluid therapy titrated to blood pressure goals is PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to give additional IM epinephrine doses (beyond initial) or dexamethasone per this guideline?
Back: No. Epinephrine up to 3 additional doses and dexamethasone are PL5.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to give IV diphenhydramine for anaphylaxis per this guideline?
Back: No. Adult PO diphenhydramine is PL2; IV diphenhydramine (and non-PO routes in the IV section) is PL4 and above.

Front: What clinical management options fall within cumulative PL3 scope (PL1 through PL3) for Behavioral (Adult & Pediatric 2024)?
Back: Oxygen target SpO2 92–96%; BGL assessment; temperature assessment; verbal de-escalation; basic airway management as needed; physical restraint if needed with sedation checklist; cooling measures if needed; patient seated or head elevated 30°; if sedated—continuous cardiac, EtCO2, and SpO2 monitoring.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to establish vascular access for a behavioral patient if indicated?
Back: No. Vascular access is PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to give IV isotonic crystalloid for a behavioral patient per this guideline?
Back: No. Fluid therapy with isotonic crystalloid is PL4 and above.

Front: Is a PL3 provider allowed to obtain a 12-lead ECG or give midazolam/droperidol for agitation per the Behavioral guideline?
Back: No. 12-lead ECG and sedation medications (midazolam, droperidol) per COG are PL5.
